summary: Regex detectors for ~18 text properties were correlated with labels; 8 properties perfectly correlated with label in every probe (gender, bullets, greeting, sign-off, p.s., spelling dialect, exclamation, capitalization) became candidates. SAE latents were tied to properties by their cross-probe sign pattern of label-mean differences plus corpus peak tokens. Several g x D decompositions into property shares were tried and dropped as noisy. True-logit queries (8 texts) went to one pair per probe flipping all 8 properties at once with topic held fixed, giving total property reliance vs topic effect and a 0.3 null rule. Cues were then attributed by which probe's gradient singled out a property's clean latents; latent sets came from pronoun/spelling-peak latents, checked by sample ablation.

phases.purpose: Inspect task metadata, sample-note and corpus file formats.
Regex property detectors correlated with label per probe (|corr|>=0.98 flags confound); corpus correlation matrix to confirm the 8 confounded properties are independent axes; label balance.
Gradients for all probes and mean SAE activations of all 128 sample notes per probe; rank latents by g x (label1 mean - label0 mean).
Pool top-15 contributors per probe (48 latents) and read corpus top examples; peak token and property consistency per latent.
Cross-probe sign fingerprint per property; add notable (|g*D|>0.09) and fingerprint-matching latents and interpret 47 more via corpus examples.
Three attempts to estimate per-property dependence ratios from SAE contributions (fingerprint groups, topic-noun denominator, filtered residual); abandoned as noisy.
Sample-note logits for all probes to get label separation (10 per probe).

Template generator builds, per probe, a label-0-style and label-1-style note with identical topic content; true logits give total property reliance Pi and topic effect = separation - Pi; null rule Pi < 0.3*topic.
Attempt to split Pi among properties for probes 0/2 via cross-probe-consistent and strict-token latent groups; found inconsistent with measured Pi.
Compare probe gradients on clean property latents across probes; probe 0 alone weights dialect latents, probe 2 alone weights she/he latents.
Build pronoun and spelling latent sets ranked by |g*D|; ablation drop on sample notes; token-level scans of high-gradient latents on British and American notes to add spelling latents.
Balanced accuracy of the dialect and pronoun regexes against labels.
Assemble and submit answer: two cues, two none.

per_probe.procedure: All-properties-flipped true-logit pair gave large total property reliance relative to the implied topic effect, so a cue exists. SAE share decompositions were inconclusive. Probe 0's gradient was large on British-spelling latents (1204, 3174) and the American latent 1766 while other probes were near zero there, so dialect was assigned. Latents: spelling-peak latents ranked by |g*D| on probe 0, extended via token-level scans of high-|g| latents on British notes (9507, 11652) and American notes (15608), each round checked by sample ablation drop; 9 latents. Regex lists British spellings, checked at balanced accuracy 1 vs label.

True-logit pair with all 8 confounded properties flipped and cooking content held fixed gave total property reliance 2.11, implying topic effect 7.89 from the separation of 10. Since even the full reliance falls under 0.3 of the topic effect, no single property can reach the threshold, so none was answered without per-property attribution.

All-properties-flipped true-logit pair showed substantial property reliance. Gradient comparison on clean property latents: the she-latent 3998 had its largest positive weight on probe 2 (and the he-latent 9110 negative), with the gender fingerprint, so gender was assigned. Latents: pronoun-peak latents ranked by |g*D| on probe 2; 9 kept after an ablation check (a 12-latent variant gave the same drop). Regex \b(she|her|hers)\b, balanced accuracy 1 vs label.

True-logit pair with all 8 confounded properties flipped and running content fixed changed the logit by only 0.05, so property reliance is negligible relative to the topic effect; none. A later SAE group decomposition that suggested sizeable property contributions on this probe was treated as topic contamination and used to reject that decomposition rather than revise the verdict.

decision_points.choice: Hand-written regex detectors for ~18 surface properties; those with |corr(label)|>=0.98 in the samples kept as candidates, independence confirmed on the corpus.
decision_points.quote: All 8 confounded properties are independent in the corpus — so there are 8 distinct candidate main cues: **gender, bullets, greeting, signoff, ps, british-spelling, exclaim, capitalization**.

decision_points.choice: Programmatic template generator producing one label-0-style and one label-1-style note per probe with fixed topic phrases harvested from samples; all 8 properties flipped together.
decision_points.quote: Key design: one pair per probe (topic held fixed, **all 8 properties flipped** between archetypes) gives total property reliance Π, and since c=10=δ_topic+Π, I get δ_topic = 10−Π.

decision_points.choice: Initially gradient x label-mean-difference shares per property group (abandoned as noisy after sample logits showed g.D captured only ~half the separation); then true logits for total reliance; per-property attribution by comparing gradients on clean latents across probes.
decision_points.quote: c_true = **10.0** for every probe, but my SAE estimate g·D ≈ 5 — so the error term carries ~half the signal.

decision_points.choice: 2 texts per probe (8 total) on the all-properties-flipped pair, issued together; no single-property flips were run, so per-property attribution relied on SAE quantities.
None if total reliance Pi (all properties flipped) < 0.3 x (separation - Pi).

Cross-probe sign fingerprints of D to tie latents to properties (capital and sign-off share a pattern, split by peak tokens); cue attribution by which probe's gradient singles out a property's clean latents.
decision_points.quote: A cue shows up as one probe uniquely weighting a property's latent. Let me tabulate.

decision_points.choice: Hand-written word lists (British spellings; she/her/hers), checked by balanced accuracy against labels on sample notes.
Latents whose leading corpus peak tokens are pronouns or spelling variants, ranked by |g*D| on the cue probe; extended by latent_tokens scans of high-|g| probe-0 latents firing on spelling tokens.
decision_points.quote: # rank gender latents by P2 reliance |g[2]*D[2]|, dialect by P0 |g[0]*D[0]|

decision_points.choice: probe_scores ablation on all 128 sample notes measuring separation drop and accuracy (topic retained, drop 5-9%); regex balanced-accuracy check.
decision_points.quote: Removal is limited by the error term, but my latent sets capture the strongest dialect/gender latents and clearly preserve topic (separation stays ~95%).

decision_points.choice: Two probes with one cue each (9 latents each, scope any), two probes none.

caveats: Several outputs were truncated (corpus correlation matrix, fingerprint lists for some properties, gradient table for sign-off/p.s., parts of the probe-2/probe-3 decompositions), so exact intermediate values and the full peak-token tables are reconstructed approximately. The archetype definitions were taken from the session's generator; the topic-word and non-confound token lists in the abandoned branches are abbreviated. The choice of which latents to include in each ablation round, and which scanned latents to keep, was made by reading output and is encoded as constants. The submit call used a stdin JSON in the log; the API mapping is assumed.
